title: Retired Army vet, no coding background. 250 iterations with Claude got me from a 17KB prototype to a shipped 130KB tank game
author: MDawg74
selftext:
Vibe Tanks, free browser game, no ads or accounts. What the AI workflow actually looked like: I acted as director and QA, never touched the code directly. Every feature went spec, build, headless test harness, my device testing, then rollback or ship. Kept a byte-identical backup before every change.

Hard lessons: AI happily ships silent bugs (a compressor node recursing into itself killed performance for days until I made it hunt with instrumentation), naming collisions between systems, and double-offset math in touch controls. The fix discipline was always the same: reproduce, isolate, verify with a test, then patch.

Original 17KB prototype vs today: same core philosophy, equal tanks and pure skill, but now with a 60Hz deterministic sim, synthesized adaptive soundtrack, stats, trophies, PWA install.

Game: [hammeranvilbrew.com/vibetanks?utm\_source=r\_aigamedev](http://hammeranvilbrew.com/vibetanks?utm_source=r_aigamedev)

Happy to detail any part of the workflow.

replies.author: MDawg74
replies.body: Thank you. I am really going for a competitive balance with it. So while there aren't many weapons or backgrounds yet, the game should feel fun every time someone plays. Once I get people interested, I plan to make it online multiplayer.

comments.author: loontoon
comments.body: Nice!  That looks fun and I love the retro style. It reminds me of fun games I played in the 80s.

replies.author: MDawg74
replies.body: Thank you! Hit the link and give it a try. I'll be happy to get any feedback.

replies.author: loontoon
replies.body:
Your link doesn't work (Chrome).  I had to type hammeranvilbrew into google to find a working link.

I've just tried the game and probably because I don't play games myself, I found it really hard.   
  
I don't have the gamer muscle memory to control the tank (WASD) and also aim the mouse.... I was looking at the keyboard all the time to see which key I needed to press.  

I'm sure people who are used to that style of control would be all over it.  

Is there any reason you have the game open full screen?  I used a 50" 4K screen and sit about 12" from it.  Fullscreen is unplayable for me, but I discovered esc switched back to a browser window. 

Despite those issues, which are me issues, I think its a cool game!

replies.author: MDawg74
replies.body: Thanks, that's exactly the feedback I need. Link should be [https://www.hammeranvilbrew.com/vibetanks](https://www.hammeranvilbrew.com/vibetanks) I am checking why the bare link failed. Fullscreen point is fair, ESC exits it, and I'm rethinking auto-fullscreen on desktop. Difficulty has an EASY setting under LEVEL on the menu, sounds like I need to surface it better. At first, I also found a little difficulty playing it, but i was able to adapt after awhile. I think part of the fun is learning the skill. 50" would be a formidable screen to do full!

comments.author: Cielu1
comments.body: It hase some UX issues, that if were fixed would make the game great :D

replies.author: MDawg74
replies.body: Please elaborate. Be specific. I will fix them if I can. The feedback button in game will work best, but I can try to answer here too.

replies.author: Cielu1
replies.body:
Its just lot of basic game-design  knowledge to be applied there , claude can generate something looking liek a game, but not actual a game. Same like LLM can write something that looks liek a book but it's not real book. It's the part of human "art".  
Basically stuff like:  
\- Player Feedback: i dont know which way I am driving, because front of tank is same as back, so i was driving backwards all game  
\-  Player UX: no "hold button" on mouse , so clicking every time to shoot is annoying   
\- Player feedback: Shoots dont feel heavy, it should have an effect on scene / tank   
\- The obstacles are too flashy, they look like targets to hit . 

Go ask your LLM about "FEEL" in game :)   
And include it in your prompts

replies.author: MDawg74
replies.body: I'll take a look at it all. Thanks.
